solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: All the letters of Plath Bea devoured

indicators.note: something devoured is torn apart and broken up, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: A writer named Bea gobbles up every letter of the poet Plath's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the complete set of letters used to write a language.

clue.text: Old storyteller regularly made use of PA

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one, across the words made use of PA

explanation.surface: An ancient teller of tales used a public address system to reach his audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the Greek slave of antiquity credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: Impressive display of work left in Pennsylvania and New York

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: the words for work and left sit inside the letters for the city

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A grand exhibition of labour is mounted in two north-eastern American states.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is a splendid array or full ceremonial show of things.

clue.text: Doctor hasn't mobile, leading to cancellation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician without a mobile phone finds appointments called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is a verb meaning tamper with, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolishment is the act of doing away with something, a cancellation of it.

clue.text: Undoubtedly like one to visit cathedral city

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so these letters are placed within the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
as means like, in 'as good as gold'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone apparently certain that a single person will go and see a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily can mean without question, as in 'easily the best', so it serves for undoubtedly.

clue.text: A long time back for example visiting S Africa

indicators.note: back says the letters built here are read in reverse order
a visitor goes in, so the example abbreviation sits inside the letters S and A

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Africa
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: It took ages for someone to come back from a trip to South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole of SEGA (EG inside SA), not just the EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal idiom for a very lengthy period, as in 'I waited ages'.

clue.text: Third grade glossy turned over by graduate

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means the word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a glossy is a glossy magazine, a MAG
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A third-class mark on a shiny paper is overturned by someone with a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third Greek letter, used for a third-class mark in marking schemes.

clue.text: Devious US uni, so in need of reform

indicators.note: something in need of reform must be reshaped, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked American university is therefore crying out for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuous means winding, and devious can likewise mean twisting or roundabout in course.

clue.text: Biblical book, or endless ditty performed by a single monk?

parts.note: a ditty is a short song
a song of someone is one by them, so of stands for performed by
a solo is something done by a single performer

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the whole phrase is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word monk itself

explanation.surface: Either a book of the Bible, or a little tune sung solo by a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Solomon, also called the Song of Songs, is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Card held by bridge player in need of a partner?

definitions.text: Card held by bridge player in need of a partner?

parts.words: Card held by bridge player in need of a partner?
parts.note: pictures a single card of the red suit with no companion in a bridge hand, and also a person seeking a mate

explanation.surface: A bridge player holds a card and wants someone to play with.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, partners matter; a lone card of one suit is pictured as a heart longing for company, the term for someone single and seeking romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely heart is a person, often advertising in personal columns, looking for a romantic companion.

clue.text: After gym, sip fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters follow the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling and agitation, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: After a workout, take sips of a bubbly drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsi is a well-known brand of carbonated cola, a non-alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Pine, silver, originally orange in the distant past

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of the word orange

explanation.surface: A pine tree, silver and orange colours seen in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago is an idiom for a time far back in history.

clue.text: Reaper, gutless: sarcastic, yet handsome

indicators.note: gutless means each word loses its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cowardly reaper with a mocking tongue who is nonetheless good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' looks like a description of the reaper's courage, but it strips sarcastic, yet and handsome to SC, YT and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is the long-bladed tool for cutting crops, so it can stand for a reaper.

clue.text: Separate ends of shop illuminated

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters, here of shop

parts.note: something illuminated is lit up

explanation.surface: The far parts of a store are brightly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate, as a couple or group parting ways.

clue.text: Name of female in Grammar School?

indicators.note: the woman's word is placed inside the school's initials

parts.note: a lady is a female

explanation.surface: Asking what a girl at a selective school is called.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school in Britain is a state secondary school that selects pupils by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a woman's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Blue duo cavorting in capital of Wisconsin

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about wildly, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad pair of performers frolicking in the main city of a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Wisconsin' is not Madison but the capital letter at the front of the word: W, spelt out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin begins with a capital W, and the letter W is named double-u.

clue.text: I'm said to make you smile: the stuff of dreams?

definitions.text: I'm said to make you smile
definitions.meaning: photographers tell subjects to say ... so they grin
eating ... at night is popularly said to cause vivid dreams

explanation.definitionFit: Saying this dairy word shapes the mouth into a grin, and folklore blames it for nightmares.

clue.text: Wooden strip containing medal found in London borough

indicators.note: the strip of wood holds the medal's letters inside it

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, with a medal

explanation.surface: A wooden slat holding an award has turned up somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour; LAMBETH is a borough of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is one of the administrative boroughs of south London, on the Thames.

clue.text: Picture held up by popular umpire

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means carried within, so the picture sits among the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An image raised aloft by a well-liked match official.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hiding no indicator; 'by' supplies it, and 'held up' reads LARUM upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a painting done directly on a wall, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Dog seen in Soho, undernourished

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are visible inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A starving dog spotted in the Soho district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound is a dog, especially one bred for hunting.

clue.text: Sleep after swallowing tablet and lots of medicine?

indicators.note: the word for sleep takes in the tablet, which sits inside it

parts.note: to doss is a British slang word for sleep, often rough
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Nodding off after taking a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSS is British slang for sleeping, often rough; E is slang for an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured quantities of a drug, so several of them are lots of medicine.

clue.text: Hunters battle, frantically, to go from disadvantage to advantage?

definitions.text: to go from disadvantage to advantage?

indicators.note: acting frantically is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Hunters fighting desperately to reverse a losing position.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is an idiom for reversing a situation so the underdog gains the upper hand.

clue.text: Minor mistake to knock back this beer?

indicators.note: to knock back is to reverse, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a slip is a minor mistake

explanation.surface: A small error to down this drink in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like drinking the beer; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager beer.

clue.text: Nearly one hundred years to capture a small race of "horsemen"

indicators.note: capturing means taking something in, so the a sits inside the shortened word
nearly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a century is a hundred years

explanation.surface: Almost a century to catch a little group of riders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' makes CENTUR from CENTURY; 'to capture' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs are mythical beings, half man and half horse, hence horsemen in quotes.
